plaintiff.occupation_after: not expected to take up any work or occupation.

injuries.description: A clinical diagnosis of right cerebral contusion was made
source: A clinical diagnosis of right cerebral contusion was made

injuries.description: On 14.1.76, a right temporoparietal craniotomy was done with a spiration of right intracerebral haemstoma.
source: On 14.1.76, a right temporoparietal craniotomy was done with a spiration of right intracerebral haemstoma.

injuries.description: x-ray of lumbar spine revealed a compression fracture of L1 vertabra.
source: x-ray of lumbar spine revealed a compression fracture of L1 vertabra.

injuries.body_part: left side of body / left limbs
source: As a result of this injury the plaintiff had residual left hemiplegia and post traumatic epilepsy which was controlled with anticonvulsant.
residual left hemiplegia

injuries.description: post traumatic epilepsy which was controlled with anticonvulsant.
source: As a result of this injury the plaintiff had residual left hemiplegia and post traumatic epilepsy which was controlled with anticonvulsant.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

injuries.description: infarction involving right anterior cerebral and middle cerebral arteries territories.
source: A C. T. brain scan showed infarction involving right anterior cerebral and middle cerebral arteries territories.

injuries.description: There was clearly damage to the Visual Perception System. There was no doubt in his mind that the plaintiff had suffered a severe visual disability in both eyes following injuries received in the accident on December 28, 1975.
injuries.body_part: visual perception system / both eyes (intracranial visual system)
source: there was no doubt in his mind that the plaintiff had suffered a severe visual disability in both eyes following injuries received in the accident on December 28, 1975. There was clearly damage to the Visual Perception System.

injuries.description: the plaintiff also suffers from left homonymous hemianopia which is a loss of vision on the left side of each eye.
source: the plaintiff also suffers from left homonymous hemianopia which is a loss of vision on the left side of each eye.

injuries.description: There was upper motor neurone type of left facial palsy
injuries.body_part: left face / facial nerve (upper motor neurone type)
source: There was upper motor neurone type of left facial palsy and left hemiparesis with left extensor plantar response.

injuries.description: incontinence of urine and faeces, initially
source: incontinence of urine and faeces, initially

injuries.description: flexion contracture of his left elbow
source: he also has a flexion contracture of his left elbow.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of other flexor muscle, fascia or tendon at forearm level

injuries.description: The most notable injury is the loss of most of his teeth.
source: The most notable injury is the loss of most of his teeth.
the damage to and lack of control of the plaintiff's right limbs were, in Dr. Lee's view, were due to lack of use over the years resulting in the limbs becoming wasted.

manifestations.description: attacks of left sided convulsions
incontinence of urine and faeces
fits of violence
mild left side headache associated with vertigo
left limbs were very spastic with marked clonus
He could just manage to walk about in his quarters with the help of a stick.
walking was now impossible
He spoke with a slurred voice, response was very slow.
He claimed that he was not able to see well and made mistakes in counting fingers placed 3 feet from him.
His right eye could not move towards the left side.
His left arm was stiff and useless. He was able to move and lift it up a few inches.
He had a tube connecting his penis to a receptacle as he was not able to control his bowel and his bladder.
His speech is incomprehensible except to those who spend a long time in his company.
He could see from a distance of two feet, one or two fingers on both eyes.
Both sides of his face were symmetrical. He did not have a normal facial expression, that is to say his face was expressionless.
The Vestibular Nerve was disturbed and consequently, he felt giddyness.
His tongue could protrude towards the left side but he had difficulty in protruding to the right side.
Jerks were not elicited over either side and ankle jerks were not elicited over either ankle.
The plaintiff's personal hygiene was very bad in Tsz Wan Shan when Dr. Lee visited them there.
capability to feed himself has been described as similar to a nine or ten month old child.

source: he was initially treated conservatively by head injury observation and the laceration was sutured.
a cerebral angiogram was done on 9.1.76

treatments_received.treatment: right temporoparietal craniotomy with aspiration of right intracerebral haemstoma
source: On 14.1.76, a right temporoparietal craniotomy was done with a spiration of right intracerebral haemstoma.

source: subsequently the plaintiff made a steady recovery and was discharged to Kowloon Hospital on 6.2.76 for convalescence and physiotherapy.
He was treated and discharged on or about the 26th November 1983 on treatment by anti-convulsant and anti-hypersensitive agents.

treatments_received.treatment: urethral catheter / tube connecting penis to receptacle
source: He had a tube connecting his penis to a receptacle as he was not able to control his bowel and his bladder.

source: He is attended 8 hours per day by a registered nurse. This is a man called Mr. Tsui.

losses.description: partial tetraplegic. His left side is hemiplegic and his right side is wasted.
The plaintiff was unable to walk
the plaintiff would require full time care and attention either at home or in an institution for the rest of his life.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: He cannot perform any function for himself. His capability to feed himself has been described as similar to a nine or ten month old child.
His speech is incomprehensible except to those who spend a long time in his company.
the plaintiff had suffered a severe visual disability in both eyes ... the visual defect in each eye was in the order of some 60 to 70% and was permanent.

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
